nodes.label: Token anatomy: ~90% of a run is thinking
nodes.rationale: Measured 2,588 plan tokens against 27,349 total output; since cost is ~96% output, schema trimming caps at 9.5% and effort/thinking are the only levers worth pulling.

nodes.label: Prompt caching works but is economically immaterial
nodes.rationale: 1,286 cached tokens against a $0.465 run saves 0.75%, a wasted write costs 0.21%; caching only matters on repair rounds and there were zero repair rounds across all 12 baseline runs.

nodes.label: Constraint density drives spend, not fixture count
nodes.rationale: teams-15 has five more fixtures than individuals-50 but 2.3x the output tokens, so any adaptive-effort heuristic must key on density (rest, blackouts, cross-person links, round-robin structure), never on movableIds.size.

nodes.label: SCHEDULING_AI_EFFORT reverted to high
nodes.rationale: Quality was identical across all 12 runs so only latency and money remain, and medium is 2.2x slower on dense packs to save $0.135 against a lifetime-capped quota; the earlier 'medium is 5.1x faster' claim came from a single 1094.9s outlier.

nodes.label: n=1 orders, n=3 sizes the gap
nodes.rationale: An n=1 outlier drove a default change that shipped for a day before repeats caught it — the clearest argument in the corpus for repeating a measurement before acting on it.

nodes.label: SCHEDULING_AI_ROUND_TIMEOUT_MS = 600s
nodes.rationale: A 1095s round demonstrably exists; the abort is client-side so raising it does not increase generation, only whether the round is received — and a timed-out run books $0.00 because the SDK reports no usage on abort.

nodes.label: Cheap-model escalation (haiku), opt-in and OFF
nodes.rationale: Haiku matches sonnet exactly on the sparse pack at 4.5x cheaper but on the dense pack stays legal while ignoring soft constraints (20–100 warnings vs 0); the warning-ratio threshold is uncalibrated, so escalation runs on referee output rather than predicting from the pack.

nodes.label: Disabling thinking fails on dense packs
nodes.rationale: Two of three no-think runs exhausted the repair loop with blocking conflicts left, and cost MORE than a clean run because each repair round re-sends the prior output as input — inverting the 'input is <4% of spend' rule to 57%.

nodes.label: schedule-ai-effort-ab.live.test.ts harness
nodes.rationale: Skipped unless AI_AB_LIVE=1 so CI never spends; runAiPlan is pure over its pack so packs are built in-file with deterministic ids and both arms of a comparison see a byte-identical pack.

nodes.label: teams-15 dense bench pack
nodes.rationale: 30 fixtures, 15 teams in 3 pools, 3 courts, 60m rest, no back-to-back, midday blackout — chosen to differ from the other pack in constraint density, not size.

nodes.label: individuals-50 sparse bench pack
nodes.rationale: 25 fixtures, 50 entrants R1 knockout, 4 courts, 10 dual-entered players so cross-person clash is the binding constraint.

nodes.label: ai-pricing.ts introductory-rate accounting
nodes.rationale: sonnet-5 is priced at the intro $2/$10 per MTok through 2026-08-31 with automatic fallback to $3/$15; costs stamped before 2026-07-20 used list and overstate spend by ~33%.
